title: Billy Douglas's original trumpet style
summary: Albert argues Billy Douglas was no copyist and had an original style, even in his arrangements, despite claims he copied Cuban Bennett or Jabbo Smith. Douglas arranged Liza.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Better do a little more talking, Dick, so... Yeah, yeah. Well, tell me about this piano and everything. Well, this is Lord Glenn. I guess Billy Douglas comes back on this. It's Dean Taylor. Yeah. It's Billy Douglas back in. And you can hear the drum back as Albert Fastmore.
Now, you know, I would have thought that he'd played more like Louie on this without hearing the record. But he wasn't just... Who is this, Billy?

Yeah, he was no copyist. No, no, no. It's just an original style. A lot of guys say he copied after some unknown trumpet player that I didn't ever hear of. Yeah. Jabo Spitt, but Jabo never played that style of trumpet. This guy's original in everything he did, even including his arrangements.
Well, Alvin told me that he liked Cuban Bennett a lot.

That's the fellow I'm referring to, but I've never heard of Cuban Bennett. But they claim he had this type of trumpet that he played. Well, if Billy Douglas copied it, he did an awful, tremendous job of copying so much.
One more, maybe. See what's next. We'll have time for one more.
Liza. That's Liza. That's an old number that was Billy Douglas arranged this one.
